issues.display_title: Issue #79: Exclude Test Accounts and Add Missing Static Routes to sitemap.xml
issues.main_description_html:
Description:

Update the automated sitemap generator for 360photographers.org to exclude test user profiles and explicitly include essential static pages (/about, /contact).

Acceptance Criteria:

  1. Filter out flag/is_test database records from the dynamic photographer URL generator in sitemap.xml.
  2. Add permanent static URL nodes for
    [https://360photographers.org/about]
    (https://360photographers.org/about)
    and
    [https://360photographers.org/contact]
    (https://360photographers.org/contact).

Result from Developer

Checked this against the live database before writing any filter, and the data says the users.test flag is not the right signal for this issue.

gothru_mod.users.test distribution

test users
0 55437
1 28
2 1
4 9
7 81

No NULLs. Values 3, 5, 6, 8 are unused.

What excluding test <> '0' would actually do

Joined against 360directory.photographers (165 published profiles today):

test photographer rows published (status 3/4)
1 8 3
2 0 0
4 0 0
7 17 7

That is 10 of 165 published profiles removed — 6% of the directory. And they do not look like test data: zero test-shaped slugs among them, 9 of 10 have avatars, 7 of 10 have websites, and one has real reviews.

Meanwhile the flag misses the actual test account

Six photographer rows have genuinely test-shaped slugs (test-, -test-, test-acc). Five are unpublished. One is live:

slug = test-address-nlxn
gothru_user_id = 54362
users.test = 0

I pulled all 165 slugs directly from GET /v2/photographers/users — test-address-nlxn is in the public directory right now, and would be published into sitemap.xml. users.test = '0', so a test <> '0' filter does not touch it.

So the flag would delete 10 real-looking profiles and still leave the one real test profile listed. It reads more like a gothru-side account categorisation than a directory test marker — whoever owns that column should confirm what 1, 2, 4 and 7 mean.

Where the sitemap leak actually came from

Not the test flag. sitemap.xml was generated from the v1 photographer list, the last caller left on that endpoint. v1 returns unpublished rows and overlapping pages, which is why test profiles appeared there: of 337 URLs, 123 were duplicates and 120 returned HTTP 404.

GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#34 switches the generator to v2 and deduplicates. v2's existing status IN (3,4) filter already drops five of the six test-slug rows, and the sitemap goes to 210 unique URLs with 202 returning 200.

Suggested resolution

  1. AC2 (static routes) — done in GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#34: /about and /contact are in the sitemap, both returning 200.
  2. AC1 (no test profiles) — effectively closed by the same PR, with one exception: test-address-nlxn needs its status changed so it leaves the directory. That is an ops action, no code required.
  3. No users.test filter. I built and tested one (shared helper, nine public readers, sqlmock tests, all green) and am not proposing it — on this data it costs 10 real profiles and fixes nothing the v2 switch did not already fix. If a durable marker is wanted, an explicit is_test column on 360directory.photographers that ops can set would be the honest version, but that is a separate issue.

The remaining 8 sitemap URLs that still 404 are unrelated to test accounts — non-ASCII slugs, filed as #81.

issues.display_title: Issue #80: Include Valid Country Directory Landing URLs in Sitemap Generator
issues.main_description_html:
Description:

Extend the sitemap generator to include country-specific directory URLs (e.g.,
[https://360photographers.org/?country=Canada]
(https://360photographers.org/?country=Canada)
or canonical country routes) to boost search engine indexing.

Acceptance Criteria:

1.Query active countries with published photographers and automatically generate corresponding sitemap entries.
2. Validate XML formatting and ensure all generated URLs return HTTP 200 responses.
